Hi Eva — thanks for the context. Quick technical summary and recommended plan (30k ft):

EU Data Residency options (pros/cons):
- Hosted EU region (recommended for speed): data-at-rest kept in eu-west storage, request bodies routed through EU-only nodes. We provide DPA and encryption keys managed by Redwood; we can also support customer-managed KMS for added controls.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full network isolation; better for audit/regulatory regimes but adds onboarding (~4–6 weeks) and higher monthly platform fee.

Cross-region failover design:
- Primary in EU (eu-west-1), warm standby in APAC region(s).
- KV cache replication: asynchronous replication to standby to enable session continuity.
- Failover mode: automated routing + warm instance promotion; expected RTO ~2–8 minutes depending on active session reconvergence.

APAC capacity recommendations:
- Dedicated APAC pool (recommended for production patient loads): reserve N GPUs to meet concurrent request SLAs; configure autoscaling buffer (20% baseline) and burst credits for seasonal peaks.
- If you prefer lower cost initially: hybrid approach — Hosted APAC + Dedicated burst for predicted peak windows.

Approximate cost bands (very high level):
- EU-hosted residency add-on: +10–20% on hosted consumption (depends on retention/GLS)
- Dedicated APAC (12-mo commitment): starting $XXk/mo for moderate workload; exact quote after capacity sizing
- Cross-region failover (warm standby): +15–30% depending on standby sizing and replication SLA

Attachments: eu-architecture-diagram.png, capacity-projection.xlsx (ballpark numbers).

I'll prepare a short config doc for your team and can join procurement calls. Proposed technical call slots: May 18 08:00–10:00 SGT / May 17 22:00 UTC.
